IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered — service="inference-proxy-eu-west1" severity=HIGH trigger=synthetic_canary_latency (threshold=500ms, count=3) Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345
Sam H: Acked on PD, I'm checking canary and proxy graphs
Priya R: I see a sharp latency blip from the eu-west1 synthetic job at ~11:41:50 UTC, spike ~520-700ms for ~90s
Jorge M: No 5xxs in front proxy logs or downstream model pods, CPU/mem on infra nodes look normal
Sam H: Grabbed the canary output: `curl -s -w "%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null https://canary-eu-west1/health` — two runs show 0.52 and 0.61s
Priya R: IncidentBot just auto-resolved PD (INC12345) — resolution reason: metric returned below threshold for rolling window
Sam H: Confirming no customer error-rate bump in the last 15m. No user-facing impact detected :white_check_mark:
Jorge M: Looks like noisy synthetic probe or temporary network hiccup between probe runner and infra; correlates with scheduled canary job (no overlap with deploys)
Alice L: Can we add jitter to canary schedule? these periodic probes cluster on the minute sometimes and trip tight thresholds
Sam H: Filing follow-up: MON-7123 created — "Tune synthetic canary alerting + add jitter/backoff" assigned to @Alice L. Notes: consider raising threshold to 700ms for eu-west1 non-prod probe
Alice L: I'll triage MON-7123 tomorrow, and check the synthetic runner CPU (observed spike to ~85% during the window)
Mike T: On-call handover: @Mike T is now watching, no active customer impact; ping me if it reappears :eyes:
Sam H: Quick debug snippet I ran: `kubectl logs -n canary canary-runner-xyz | grep "latency"` — shows short-lived DNS timeouts at 11:41:49-11:42:20
Jorge M: Added small runbook note in the monitoring doc about noisy synthetic runs and suggested backoff strategy
Priya R: Marking thread as no-customer-impact and resolved. Recommend follow-up before next business day
IncidentBot: Thread metadata updated: tags=[auto-resolved, no-customer-impact, synthetic-canary]
__note: This document is a single Slack thread string. Messages are in chronological order and each line is prefixed with the sender's display name.
